# dsh-memory-lite
Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), scoped by workspace directory. Sessions opened in the s
ame directory share one memory store; sessions in a different directory see none of it, except for m
emories saved with the `global` scope. Every memory is a plain Markdown file on disk. No network req
uests, no automatic model calls, no database, no index files.
## Features

- Five tools: `memory_save`, `memory_search`, `memory_get`, `memory_list`, `memory_forget`
- A short
"title index" section injected into the system prompt when a session starts, so the agent knows wha

t exists without reading every file
- Workspace isolation keyed by the normalized working directory

- Plain Markdown with YAML front matter; readable and editable in any text editor
- Archive-on-forge

t instead of deletion
- Zero network activity, asserted by the test suite
## Requirements
- DSH Desktop 2.0.18 with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 0.2.1-rc.2 (`engines.dsh` is pinned to `>=0.2.1-rc.2

<0.2.2`)
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 4.0.5
- Node.js >= 20
- pnpm (for building from source)
## Install
From a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or directly from GitHub:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both forms register the plugin in the profile named by `--profile` (for example `desktop`) and appen
d `dsh-memory-lite` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. Restart the client if a newly created session does not
see the `memory_*` tools. Full instructions, including verification, upgrade, and uninstall, are in
INSTALL.md (Chinese).
## Tools
| Tool | Key inputs | Returns | Notes |
| `memory_save` | `title` (<= 80 chars), `body`, `scope?` (`project` \| `global`), `tags?`, `confide
nce?` | `id`, `path`, `scope` | Defaults to `project`. Rejects bodies that look like credentials. |
| `memory_search` | `query`, `scope?` (`both` \| `project` \| `global`), `limit?` | hit list with sn
ippets | Lexical scoring: title x3, tags x2, body x1. CJK text is matched as bigrams. Default limit

8, max 50. |
| `memory_get` | `id` | full record | Errors when not found; never returns empty. |
| `

memory_list` | `scope?` | title index lines | Titles only; bodies are not read. |
| `memory_forget`
| `id` | `archivedPath` | Moves the file to `.archive/`; reversible by moving it back. |
`memory_get` and `memory_forget` only reach memories visible to the current workspace plus `global`;
an id from another workspace cannot be read or archived.
## Workspace isolation
- The project key is `sha256(normalizePath(cwd)).slice(0, 12)`. `normalizePath` lowercases the drive
letter, converts `\` to `/`, collapses repeated separators, and drops the trailing separator. Symli

nks are not resolved, so renaming a directory means a new project.
- Sessions in the same directory

share the same set of project memories.
- Sessions in a different directory cannot see, search, get,

or forget those project memories, even by id.
- `global` memories are visible from every workspace.
Set `allowGlobalScope: false` to disable writing them.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `vaultPath` | `<DSH_HOME>/memory-vault` (or `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\memory-vault` when `DSH_HOME` is u

nset) | Root directory of the vault |
| `injectStanding` | `true` | Inject the standing title index

into the system prompt |
| `standingMaxItems` | `8` | Max entries in the standing section (min 1) |

| `standingBudgetChars` | `1200` | Character budget for the standing section (min 200) |
| `allowGlo

balScope` | `true` | Allow `scope: global` in `memory_save` |
| `redactSecrets` | `true` | Reject wr
ites whose body matches credential patterns (`api_key`, `secret`, `password`, `token`, private key b

locks) |
| `maxFileBytes` | `65536` | Max size of a single memory file (min 1024) |
| `autoSavePolic
y` | `off` | Whether to register a "write policy" system prompt section that nudges the agent to sav
e notable facts proactively. `hint` enables the section; `off` registers nothing. |
Values are set through the plugin's config in `cordis.patch.yml` (either the file shipped with the p
lugin, or an id-targeted patch appended to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`). Keys that are not wri
tten fall back to the schema defaults above.
## On-disk format
The vault is a plain directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One memory is one Markdown file with YAML front matter:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Writes go through a temp file plus fsync plus rename, so a crash mid-write loses at most that one wr
ite and never leaves a truncated memory file. Files over `maxFileBytes` are rejected outright, not t
runcated. `memory_forget` moves the file into `.archive/` and stamps `archivedAt`; moving it back re
stores it. There is no index file: listing and search always read the `.md` files directly, so there
is nothing to rebuild or corrupt.
## Design trade-offs
- **No network, ever.** The plugin never calls out. `test/offline.test.ts` stubs `fetch`, `http.requ

est`, `https.request`, `net.connect`, and `dns.lookup` at runtime and asserts zero call attempts.
-
**No index, no database.** Everything is derived from the files themselves. Fewer moving parts, noth

ing to maintain, and any editor can inspect the vault.
- **Archive, don't delete.** Forgetting is re

versible, which suits long-lived memories.
- **Lexical search only.** No embeddings. Fewer false rec

alls at the cost of missing synonyms.
- **Standing section is an index, not content.** The injected

text says memories are data, not instructions, and bodies must be fetched with `memory_get`.
- **Bui
lt output is committed.** `lib/` ships in the repository so the plugin can be installed straight fro
m git without a build step.
## Limitations

- Lexical search: no semantic matching, weak on synonyms.
- Renaming a project directory orphans its

memories under the old key (they remain on disk; `project.json` records the old path).
- No update

tool: replace a memory by saving a new one and forgetting the old.
- No cross-machine sync; the vaul

t is a local directory, sync it yourself if needed.
- `engines.dsh` is pinned to a narrow range; a D
SH upgrade outside `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.2.2` skips the bundle until the range is updated (see INSTALL.md
